knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local critical-cone representation and B-differentiability of a polyhedral projector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local representation and differentiability of Euclidean projection onto a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a polyhedron. For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), there exists a neighborhood \(\mathcal N\) of \(x\) such that, with \(\mathcal C=\mathcal C_\pi(x;K)\), \[\Pi_K(y)=\Pi_K(x)+\Pi_{\mathcal C}(y-x)\qquad\forall y\in\mathcal N.\] Consequently, \[\Pi_K'(x;d)=\Pi_{\mathcal C}(d)\qquad\forall d\in\mathbb{R}^n,\] and \(\Pi_K\) is strongly B-differentiable everywhere on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the normal map by \(F_C^{\mathrm{nor}}(z)=F(P_C(z))+z-P_C(z)\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a real reflexive Banach space, let \(K\subseteq X\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(A:X\to X^*\) be monotone, hemicontinuous, and bounded on bounded sets. Suppose that for some \(u_0\in K\), \[\frac{\langle Au,u-u_0\rangle}{\lVert u\rVert}\longrightarrow +\infty\quad\text{as }u\in K,\ \lVert u\rVert\to\infty.\] Then, for every \(f\in X^*\), there exists \(u\in K\) such that \[\langle Au-f,v-u\rangle\geq0\qquad\text{for every }v\in K.\] Equivalently, \(f\in Au+N_K(u)\). If \(A\) is strictly monotone on \(K\), this solution is unique.

For all \(p,r\in H\), \[\lVert x(p)-x(r)\rVert\leq\frac{1}{\mu}\lVert p-r\rVert.\] Thus \(1/\mu\) controls absolute sensitivity to additive perturbations. When the scale of the forward operator is measured by its Lipschitz modulus \(L\), the dimensionless ratio \[\kappa:=\frac{L}{\mu}\] serves as the natural strong-monotonicity conditioning parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong monotonicity bounds additive-perturbation sensitivity by the reciprocal modulus; relative conditioning is measured by the Lipschitz-to-monotonicity ratio.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: P-property of a block multifunction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the strict blockwise P-property used in variational-inequality and equilibrium uniqueness theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat K=\prod_{i=1}^N K^i\), where \(K^i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\). A multifunction \(\Phi:\widehat K\to\mathbb R^n\) has the P-property on \(\widehat K\) if, for every pair \(\widehat x=(\widehat x^i)_{i=1}^N\ne\widetilde x=(\widetilde x^i)_{i=1}^N\) in \(\widehat K\) and every \(\widehat y=(\widehat y^i)_{i=1}^N\in\Phi(\widehat x)\), \(\widetilde y=(\widetilde y^i)_{i=1}^N\in\Phi(\widetilde x)\), one has \[\max_{1\le i\le N}(\widehat x^i-\widetilde x^i)^T(\widehat y^i-\widetilde y^i)>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block multifunction has the P-property if every two distinct domain points and every corresponding pair of multifunction values have a block with strictly positive displacement–value-difference inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{1\le i\le N}(\widehat x^i-\widetilde x^i)^T(\widehat y^i-\widetilde y^i)>0

children.title: P-Function Conditions
children.top_down_role: Global uniqueness conditions based on the P-function property.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is a P-function on \(K\) exactly when the displayed strict maximum condition holds for every distinct pair.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional coordinatewise definition on an arbitrary domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The mapping \(F\) is a P-function on \(K\) if and only if, for every distinct \(x,y\in K\), \[\max_{1\le i\le n}(x_i-y_i)\bigl(F_i(x)-F_i(y)\bigr)>0.\] Equivalently, for every \(x\ne y\), at least one coordinate simultaneously gives a strictly positive displacement and operator-difference product.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mapping is a P-function when every distinct pair has at least one coordinate whose displacement and operator change have a strictly positive product.
knowledge_statements.title: P-Function Conditions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed condition is the standard finite-dimensional definition of a P-function and the condition role fits the leaf, but no inspectable citation or authoritative locator is supplied.

children.title: Uniform P-Function Conditions
children.top_down_role: Quantitatively strengthened P-function conditions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is uniformly P on \(K\) exactly when the displayed inequality holds for some \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-growth version of the coordinatewise P condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The mapping \(F\) is a uniform P-function on \(K\) if and only if there exists \(\alpha>0\) such that, for all \(x,y\in K\), \[\max_{1\le i\le n}(x_i-y_i)\bigl(F_i(x)-F_i(y)\bigr)\ge \alpha\|x-y\|^2.\] Any admissible \(\alpha\) is a uniform P-function modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform P behavior requires the largest coordinate product to dominate the squared distance by one positive constant for every pair.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform P-Function Conditions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quadratic uniform P-function condition is precise and the condition role fits the leaf, but the record has no source supporting the selected normalization and definition.

children.title: Uniformity Strengthening Boundary
children.top_down_role: Structural distinction between ordinary and uniform P-function regimes.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is a P-function on \(K\) but is not a uniform P-function there.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete boundary showing that strict P behavior need not be uniform.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For distinct \(s,t\in K\), strict increase of \(F\) gives \((s-t)(s^3-t^3)>0\), so \(F\) is a P-function. Uniformity would require some \(\alpha>0\) satisfying \(t^4\ge\alpha t^2\) for every \(t\in K\), by comparing \(t\) with \(0\). This is impossible as nonzero \(t\to0\). Hence the implication uniform P \(\Rightarrow\) P is strict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scalar map t cubed is strictly P on a bounded interval but has no positive uniform P modulus near zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniformity Strengthening Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar example correctly separates P-function behavior from uniform P-function behavior and failure_boundary fits the terminal container. However, it has no citation and its statement includes a derivation rather than only the knowledge statement.

assumptions_latex: \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is a P-matrix, meaning every principal minor of \(M\) is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linear complementarity problem \(\operatorname{LCP}(M,q)\) has exactly one solution for every \(q\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical global unique-solvability characterization for linear complementarity problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the complementarity system \[z\ge0,\qquad w=Mz+q\ge0,\qquad \langle z,w\rangle=0.\] If \(M\) is a P-matrix, then for every \(q\in\mathbb{R}^n\) this system has a unique solution \(z\). Conversely, if the system has a unique solution for every \(q\in\mathbb{R}^n\), then \(M\) is a P-matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix is a P-matrix exactly when its linear complementarity problem has one and only one solution for every right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.title: P-Matrix Global Uniqueness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The P-matrix characterization of unique solvability of LCP(M,q) for every right-hand side is a theorem matching this topic, but no authoritative theorem or page locator is cited.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: P-Matrix Characterization by Global LCP Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform uniqueness of the LCP over all right-hand-side vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(M\) is a \(\mathbf P\)-matrix if and only if \(\operatorname{LCP}(q,M)\) has a unique solution for every \(q\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real square matrix is a P-matrix exactly when its linear complementarity problem has a unique solution for every right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\in\mathbf P\iff \forall q\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ \operatorname{LCP}(q,M)\text{ has a unique solution}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that for every distinct \(x,y\in K\), \[\max_{1\le i\le N}\langle x_i-y_i,F_i(x)-F_i(y)\rangle>0.\] Then there is at most one \(x\in K\) satisfying \[\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\qquad\text{for every }y\in K.\] The Cartesian-product structure permits each block to be varied separately and is essential to this blockwise uniqueness criterion.

children.title: P-Zero Relaxation
children.top_down_role: The weakened P-property regime based on P-zero behavior.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The P-zero condition is the nonstrict relaxation of the P-function condition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise nonstrict relaxation of the P-function predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The mapping \(F\) is a P-zero function on \(K\) if, for every distinct \(x,y\in K\), \[\max_{1\le i\le n}(x_i-y_i)\bigl(F_i(x)-F_i(y)\bigr)\ge0.\] Replacing this nonstrict inequality by strict positivity yields the P-function condition; consequently every P-function is P-zero, but the reverse implication need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A P-zero function replaces the strict positive coordinate product required of a P-function by a nonnegative one.
knowledge_statements.title: P-Zero Relaxation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonstrict coordinatewise condition correctly defines the finite-dimensional P-zero relaxation, and definition is appropriate for the leaf. No source or locator is provided.

children.title: Nonuniqueness Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes where global uniqueness can no longer be maintained.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and contains at least two points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is P-zero but not P, and every point of \(K\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(K,F)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp loss of uniqueness after strict P positivity is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any distinct \(x,y\in K\), every coordinate product \((x_i-y_i)(F_i(x)-F_i(y))\) equals \(0\). Thus \(F\) satisfies the P-zero condition but not the P-function condition. Moreover, every \(x\in K\) satisfies \[\langle F(x),y-x\rangle=0\qquad\text{for every }y\in K,\] so P-zero structure alone does not ensure uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zero mapping is P-zero, yet every feasible point solves the variational inequality, showing exactly where P-based uniqueness can fail.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonuniqueness Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The zero-map example correctly marks the loss-of-uniqueness boundary and failure_boundary is the right role. The record lacks a citation, and the statement contains explanatory derivation that should not appear in a proof-free knowledge statement.

children.title: Multiplicity under P-Zero Structure
children.top_down_role: Solution multiplicity patterns compatible with P-zero structure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solution set is \(\{0\}\times[0,1]\), although \(F\) is P-zero.

notation.meaning: solution set of the variational inequality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconstant P-zero mapping with a continuum of VI solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,y\in K\), the coordinate products are \((x_1-y_1)^2\) and \(0\), so \(F\) is P-zero. The variational inequality is \[x_1(y_1-x_1)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }y_1\in[0,1].\] This holds exactly when \(x_1=0\), while \(x_2\) is unrestricted. Hence \[\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)=\{0\}\times[0,1].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconstant P-zero mapping on the unit square can have an entire line segment of variational-inequality solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplicity under P-Zero Structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mapping is P-zero and its VI solution set is correctly stated as {0} times [0,1]; counterexample fits the multiplicity leaf. The record nevertheless has no source and includes the calculation establishing the result.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local uniqueness of a smoothly constrained VI solution and conditional characterization of locally unique KKT triples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\operatorname{VI}(K,F)\), with \(K\) represented by the stated constraint system. Let \(x\) be a solution. Assume \(F\) is continuously differentiable near \(x\), all \(h_j\) and \(g_i\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x\), and \(x\) satisfies SBCQ. If, for every \((\mu,\lambda)\in\mathcal M(x)\), the system \(\mathcal C(x;K,F)\ni v\perp J_x\mathbf L(x,\mu,\lambda)v\in\mathcal C(x;K,F)^*\) has only the solution \(v=0\), then \(x\) is locally unique. Under these assumptions, \((x,\mu,\lambda)\) is a locally unique solution of the KKT system if and only if \(\mathcal M(x)=\{(\mu,\lambda)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under SBCQ, smoothness, and zero-only solvability of every multiplier-specific homogeneous critical-cone complementarity system, the VI solution is locally unique. A KKT triple is locally unique exactly when its multiplier pair is the unique multiplier pair at that solution.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT-Triple Local Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth constrained VI; strong metric regularity gives local uniqueness of the entire primal-dual triple.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\), and \(z=(x,\lambda,\mu)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R_+^m\times\mathbb R^p\). Define \[\mathcal K(z):=\begin{pmatrix}F(x)+\nabla g(x)^\mathsf T\lambda+\nabla h(x)^\mathsf T\mu\\ h(x)\\-g(x)\end{pmatrix}+\begin{pmatrix}0\\0\\N_{\mathbb R_+^m}(\lambda)\end{pmatrix}.\] If \(0\in\mathcal K(\bar z)\) and \(\mathcal K\) is strongly metrically regular at \((\bar z,0)\), then there are neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar z\) and \(V\) of \(0\) such that \(p\mapsto\mathcal K^{-1}(p)\cap U\) is single-valued and Lipschitz on \(V\). In particular, \(\mathcal K^{-1}(0)\cap U=\{\bar z\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong metric regularity of the KKT generalized equation makes the nearby primal-dual solution single-valued and Lipschitz, so the reference KKT triple is locally unique.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
The feasible set is locally \(K=\{x:g(x)\leq0,\ h(x)=0\}\), and \(\bar z=(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R_+^m\times\mathbb R^p\) is a KKT triple.
The KKT generalized equation is strongly metrically regular at \((\bar z,0)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Map Local Invertibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-homeomorphism formulation for a finite-dimensional VI over a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z\in\mathbb R^n\), define \[F_K^{\mathrm{nor}}(z):=F(\Pi_K z)+z-\Pi_K z.\] Suppose \(F_K^{\mathrm{nor}}(\bar z)=0\) and there are neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar z\) and \(V\) of \(0\) such that \(F_K^{\mathrm{nor}}:U\to V\) is a homeomorphism. Then \(\bar z\) is the unique zero in \(U\), and \(\bar x=\Pi_K(\bar z)\) is locally unique among solutions of \(0\in F(x)+N_K(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the normal map is a local homeomorphism at a zero, that zero and its corresponding nearby variational-inequality solution are locally unique.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
The normal map is a homeomorphism between a neighborhood of its zero \(\bar z\) and a neighborhood of \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The point \(\bar x=\Pi_K(\bar z)\) is the unique solution of \(0\in F(x)+N_K(x)\) in some neighborhood of \(\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional characterization of isolated complementarity solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient B-derivative condition, with an affine converse, for isolation of a componentwise complementarity solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F,G:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be B-differentiable on the open set \(\mathcal D\), and let \(x\) solve the complementarity problem. Suppose the only \(v\) satisfying \(F_i'(x;v)=0\) for every \(i\) with \(F_i(x)=0<G_i(x)\), \(\min\{F_i'(x;v),G_i'(x;v)\}=0\) for every \(i\) with \(F_i(x)=G_i(x)=0\), and \(G_i'(x;v)=0\) for every \(i\) with \(F_i(x)>0=G_i(x)\), is \(v=0\). Then \(x\) is an isolated complementarity solution. Conversely, if \(F\) and \(G\) are affine and \(x\) is an isolated solution, then this directional system has the unique solution \(v=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the active-pattern directional system of a complementarity problem has only the zero solution, then the reference solution is isolated. For affine complementarity maps, isolation also implies this directional condition.
assumptions_latex: F,G:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\text{ are B-differentiable and }\mathcal D\text{ is open}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is isolated; if }F,G\text{ are affine, isolation is equivalent to uniqueness of }v=0\text{ in the directional system}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Critical-cone characterization of VI nondegeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes a nondegenerate VI solution through its critical cone and identifies that cone with the tangent cone's lineality space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex, let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), and let \(x\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\). Then \(x\) is nondegenerate if and only if \(\mathcal C(x;K,F)\) is a linear subspace. When these equivalent conditions hold, \(\mathcal C(x;K,F)=\operatorname{lin}\mathcal T(x;K)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded-set comparison of complementarity residuals under nondegeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: For a parametric AVI KKT system, nondegeneracy of every solution yields a uniform residual comparison on each bounded portion of the relaxed feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\) and \(\Omega\) be the relaxed feasible region and full solution set of the parametric-AVI KKT system. Suppose every \((x,y,\lambda)\in\Omega\) is nondegenerate in the componentwise sense \[\lambda-(Dx+Ey+b)>0.\] Then, for every \(\rho>0\), there exists \(\tau>0\) such that every \((x,y,\lambda)\in W\cap\mathbb{B}(0,\rho)\) satisfies \[\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\min\{\lambda_i,-(Dx+Ey+b)_i\}\leq-\tau\lambda^T(Dx+Ey+b).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every solution satisfies the stated nondegeneracy condition, then on every bounded part of the relaxed KKT region the summed minimum complementarity residual is bounded by a constant multiple of the complementarity-product residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\min\{\lambda_i,-(Dx+Ey+b)_i\}\leq-\tau\lambda^T(Dx+Ey+b)

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the complementarity system \[\bar x\geq0,\qquad \bar s=F(\bar x)\geq0,\qquad \bar x_i\bar s_i=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,n),\] define \(B(\bar x):=\{i:\bar x_i=0,\ \bar s_i=0\}\). knowledge_statements.title: Connectedness of Solution Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity consequence of convexity for a nonempty continuous monotone VI solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(F:K\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous and monotone. If \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\neq\varnothing\), then \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\) is path connected. More precisely, for all \(x^0,x^1\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\) and every \(t\in[0,1]\), \[(1-t)x^0+tx^1\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonempty solution set of a continuous monotone VI on a closed convex feasible set is path connected; the segment joining any two solutions remains in the solution set.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
The VI has at least one solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solution set \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\) is path connected, and hence connected.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete one-dimensional boundary mechanism showing that continuity alone does not ensure connected solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=[-2,2]\subset\mathbb R\) and define \(F:K\to\mathbb R\) by \(F(x)=x^2-1\). Then \[\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)=\{-2,-1,1\},\] which is disconnected. Thus continuity of \(F\) and convexity of \(K\) alone do not ensure connectedness of the VI solution set.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedrality of AVI Solution Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General affine VI over a polyhedron, with the monotone case distinguished.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedral convex set and let \(F(x)=Mx+q\). For every face \(G\) of \(K\), set \[S_G:=\{x\in G:-Mx-q\in N_K(G)\}.\] Then each \(S_G\) is a polyhedral convex set and \[\operatorname{SOL}(K,Mx+q)=\bigcup_{G\in\mathcal F(K)}S_G,\] where \(\mathcal F(K)\) is the finite face family of \(K\). If \(M\) is positive semidefinite, then the solution set is a convex polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine VI over a polyhedron has a solution set representable as a finite union of polyhedral face pieces; when the affine field is monotone, the complete solution set is a convex polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty polyhedral convex set.
The VI field is affine: \(F(x)=Mx+q\), where \(M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(q\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The AVI solution set is a finite union of polyhedral convex sets; if \(M\) is positive semidefinite, it is a convex polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Convexity and Polyhedrality Conditions for AVI Solution Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent geometric and algebraic conditions for the solution set of an affine variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M)\). The following statements are equivalent: \(S\) is convex; for every \(x^1,x^2\in S\), \((x^1)^T(q+Mx^1)=(x^2)^T(q+Mx^1)\); for every \(x^1,x^2\in S\), \((x^1-x^2)^TM(x^1-x^2)=0\); and \(S\) is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an affine variational inequality, convexity of the solution set, the stated pairwise equality, vanishing of the quadratic form on every difference of solutions, and polyhedrality of the solution set are equivalent.
assumptions_latex: \(S=\operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M)\) is the solution set of the affine variational inequality \(\operatorname{AVI}(K,q,M)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\text{ convex}\iff[\forall x^1,x^2\in S,\ (x^1)^T(q+Mx^1)=(x^2)^T(q+Mx^1)]\iff[\forall x^1,x^2\in S,\ (x^1-x^2)^TM(x^1-x^2)=0]\iff S\text{ polyhedral}.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong stability characterized by a strong B-derivative
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between strong stability of an equation and strong stability or global Lipschitz invertibility of its strong B-derivative model.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular and strongly regular isolated zeros
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local solvability and localization for right-hand-side perturbations, strengthened by single-valued Lipschitz dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^n\), where \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is open, and let \(x\in\mathcal D\) be an isolated zero of \(H\). The zero \(x\) is regular if, for every open neighborhood \(\mathcal N\) of \(x\) satisfying \(\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N\subset\mathcal D\) and \(H^{-1}(0)\cap\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N=\{x\}\), there exist an open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\) of \(0\) and \(c>0\) such that \(\varnothing\ne H^{-1}(u)\cap\mathcal N\subseteq\mathbb B(x,c\|u\|)\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\). It is strongly regular if, in addition, \(H^{-1}(u)\cap\mathcal N=\{x_{\mathcal N}(u)\}\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\) and \(\|x_{\mathcal N}(u)-x_{\mathcal N}(u')\|\le c\|u-u'\|\) for every \(u,u'\in\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularity requires every sufficiently small right-hand side to have a local solution whose displacement from the isolated zero is proportional to the perturbation. Strong regularity additionally requires that local solution to be unique and Lipschitz-continuous in the right-hand side.
assumptions_latex: \(H:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^n\) is a given map
\(x\in\mathcal D\) is an isolated zero of \(H\)
\(\mathcal N\ni x\) is open, \(\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N\subset\mathcal D\), and \(H^{-1}(0)\cap\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N=\{x\}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{regular}:\ \exists\mathcal U\ni0,\exists c>0\ \forall u\in\mathcal U,\ \varnothing\ne H^{-1}(u)\cap\mathcal N\subseteq\mathbb B(x,c\|u\|);\quad \text{strongly regular}:\ \forall u\in\mathcal U,\ H^{-1}(u)\cap\mathcal N=\{x_{\mathcal N}(u)\},\ \forall u,u'\in\mathcal U,\ \|x_{\mathcal N}(u)-x_{\mathcal N}(u')\|\le c\|u-u'\|.\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded local perturbation result for a B-differentiable variational inequality, with the source-referenced conditions (5.1.1) and (5.1.4) retained without expansion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be closed and convex, let \mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be open with K\subseteq\mathcal D, and let F:\mathcal D\to\mathbb{R}^n be B-differentiable at x^*\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent error bounds for a B-differentiable equation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between nonsingularity of the Bouligand derivative, its global homogeneous error bound, and a local residual error bound at a zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous, where \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is open. Suppose \(H(x)=0\) and \(H\) is B-differentiable at \(x\). Then the following are equivalent: (a) \(H'(x;v)=0\Rightarrow v=0\); (b) there exists \(c'>0\) such that \(\|v\|\le c'\|H'(x;v)\|\) for every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\); (c) there exist an open neighborhood \(\mathcal N\subseteq\mathcal D\) of \(x\) and \(c>0\) such that \(\|x'-x\|\le c\|H(x')\|\) for every \(x'\in\mathcal N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a zero of a continuous B-differentiable equation, trivial kernel of the B-derivative, a uniform error bound for that derivative, and a local residual error bound for the original equation are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([H'(x;v)=0\Rightarrow v=0]\iff[\exists c'>0\ \forall v\in\mathbb R^n,\ \|v\|\le c'\|H'(x;v)\|]\iff[\exists\mathcal N\ni x,\exists c>0\ \forall x'\in\mathcal N,\ \|x'-x\|\le c\|H(x')\|]\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly stable isolated zero
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong perturbation stability defined by existence of perturbed zeros and a uniform pairwise estimate for all choices of such zeros.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^n\), where \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is open, and let \(x\in\mathcal D\) be an isolated zero of \(H\). The zero \(x\) is strongly stable if, for every open neighborhood \(\mathcal N\) of \(x\) satisfying \(\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N\subset\mathcal D\) and \(H^{-1}(0)\cap\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N=\{x\}\), there exist \(c,\varepsilon>0\) such that: (a) for every \(G\in\operatorname{IB}(H;\varepsilon,\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N)\), \(G^{-1}(0)\cap\mathcal N\ne\varnothing\); and (b) for every \(G,\widetilde G\) in that class, every \(v\in G^{-1}(0)\cap\mathcal N\), and every \(\widetilde v\in\widetilde G^{-1}(0)\cap\mathcal N\), \(\|v-\widetilde v\|\le c\|H(v)-H(\widetilde v)\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An isolated zero is strongly stable when each sufficiently small perturbation has a nearby zero and every pair of nearby zeros selected from any two such perturbations satisfies the stated uniform residual comparison.
assumptions_latex: \(H:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^n\) is a given map
\(x\in\mathcal D\) is an isolated zero of \(H\)
\(\mathcal N\ni x\) is open, \(\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N\subset\mathcal D\), and \(H^{-1}(0)\cap\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N=\{x\}\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semistable and stable isolated zeros
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation definitions distinguished by whether nearby perturbed zeros are merely bounded when present or are also required to exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous, where \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is open, and let \(x\in\mathcal D\) be an isolated zero of \(H\). The zero \(x\) is semistable if, for every open neighborhood \(\mathcal N\) of \(x\) satisfying \(\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N\subset\mathcal D\) and \(H^{-1}(0)\cap\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N=\{x\}\), there exist \(\varepsilon,c>0\) such that for every \(G\in\operatorname{IB}(H;\varepsilon,\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N)\) and every \(x'\in G^{-1}(0)\cap\mathcal N\), \(\|x'-x\|\le c\|H(x')\|\). It is stable if, for every such \(\mathcal N\), there exist \(\varepsilon,c>0\) such that every such \(G\) has a zero in \(\mathcal N\) and the same inequality holds for every \(x'\in G^{-1}(0)\cap\mathcal N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semistability imposes a uniform residual bound on any nearby perturbed zeros but does not itself require such zeros to exist. Stability requires both existence and that bound for every perturbation in the stated class.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathcal D\) is an isolated zero of \(H\)
\(\mathcal N\ni x\) is open, \(\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N\subset\mathcal D\), and \(H^{-1}(0)\cap\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N=\{x\}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{semistable}:\ \forall\mathcal N\ \exists\varepsilon,c>0\ \forall G\in\operatorname{IB}(H;\varepsilon,\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N)\ \forall x'\in G^{-1}(0)\cap\mathcal N,\ \|x'-x\|\le c\|H(x')\|;\quad \text{stable}:\ \text{the same bound and }G^{-1}(0)\cap\mathcal N\ne\varnothing\text{ for every }G.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stable-zero criteria via the B-derivative model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between stability of a B-differentiable equation and stability, uniqueness, and bounded-inverse properties of its directional model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be a zero of a continuous map \(H:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^n\), where \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is open. Suppose \(H\) is B-differentiable at \(x\), define \(\Gamma(y)=H'(x;y-x)\), and assume \(\Gamma\) has the nonvanishing property at \(x\). Then the following are equivalent: (a) \(x\) is a stable zero of \(\Gamma\); (b) \(\Gamma\) is surjective and \(\Gamma^{-1}(\mathbb B(0,1))\) is bounded; (c) \(x\) is the unique zero of \(\Gamma\); (d) \(x\) is a stable zero of \(H\); and (e) there exist an open neighborhood \(\mathcal N\) of \(x\) satisfying (5.2.3) and \(\varepsilon,c>0\) such that, for every \(G\in\mathbb B(H;\varepsilon,\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N)\), the set \(G^{-1}(0)\cap\mathcal N\) is nonempty and (5.2.5) holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under B-differentiability and the nonvanishing property, stability of the original zero is equivalent to stability and uniqueness for the B-derivative model, its surjectivity with bounded unit-ball preimage, and the source's stated uniform perturbation condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ stable for }\Gamma\iff[\Gamma\text{ surjective and }\Gamma^{-1}(\mathbb B(0,1))\text{ bounded}]\iff x\text{ is the unique zero of }\Gamma\iff x\text{ stable for }H\iff\text{condition (e), including (5.2.3) and (5.2.5), holds}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semistability and stability of a VI solution set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: VI-specific solution-set stability under locally uniform operator perturbations, including the singleton-solution failure boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\neq\varnothing\). For every open set \(\mathcal U\supseteq\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\), let \(K_{\mathcal U}=K\cap\operatorname{cl}\mathcal U\). The VI \((K,F)\) is semistable if there exist \(c,\varepsilon>0\) such that every \(G\in\mathbb B(F;\varepsilon,K_{\mathcal U})\) satisfies \[\operatorname{SOL}(K,G)\cap\mathcal U\subseteq\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)+c\omega\mathbb B(0,1),\qquad \omega=\sup_{x\in K_{\mathcal U}}\|G(x)-F(x)\|.\] It is stable if, in addition, \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,G)\cap\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\) for every such \(G\). The open set \(\mathcal U\) need not be bounded. If \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)=\{x^*\}\), solution-set semistability implies pointwise semistability of \(x^*\), whereas the converse can fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A VI is solution-set semistable when every open neighborhood of its nonempty solution set admits a perturbation threshold and a linear containment bound for perturbed solutions lying in that neighborhood. Stability additionally requires such a perturbed solution to exist. The neighborhood may be unbounded. For a singleton solution set, solution-set semistability implies pointwise semistability, but not conversely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists c,\varepsilon>0\ \forall G\in\mathbb B(F;\varepsilon,K_{\mathcal U}):\ \operatorname{SOL}(K,G)\cap\mathcal U\subseteq\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)+c\omega\mathbb B(0,1),\quad \omega=\sup_{x\in K_{\mathcal U}}\|G(x)-F(x)\|;\ \text{stability additionally requires }\operatorname{SOL}(K,G)\cap\mathcal U\neq\varnothing.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semistability and epsilon-solution boundedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two directional implications relating semistability, boundedness, epsilon-solution boundedness, pointwise semiregularity, and finiteness of the VI solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex, let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous, and assume \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\neq\varnothing\). (a) If \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\) is bounded and \((K,F)\) is semistable, then \((K,F)\) is \(\varepsilon\)-solution bounded for some \(\varepsilon>0\). (b) Conversely, if \((K,F)\) is \(\varepsilon\)-solution bounded for some \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\) is pointwise semiregular, then \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\) is finite and \((K,F)\) is semistable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A semistable VI with a bounded nonempty solution set is epsilon-solution bounded. Conversely, epsilon-solution boundedness together with pointwise semiregularity makes the solution set finite and yields semistability.
assumptions_latex: K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is closed and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\text{ bounded and }(K,F)\text{ semistable}\bigr]\Rightarrow\exists\varepsilon>0:\ (K,F)\text{ is }\varepsilon\text{-solution bounded};\quad \bigl[\exists\varepsilon>0:\ (K,F)\text{ is }\varepsilon\text{-solution bounded and }\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\text{ is pointwise semiregular}\bigr]\Rightarrow\bigl[\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\text{ is finite and }(K,F)\text{ is semistable}\bigr].

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex and let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous. knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Mapping Discontinuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete finite-dimensional failure of lower semicontinuity caused by solution-set expansion at the reference parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(p\in\mathbb R\), define \(S(p)=\{x\in K:\langle F(x,p),y-x\rangle\geq0\text{ for every }y\in K\}\). Then \[S(p)=\begin{cases}\{-1\},&p>0,\\[-1,1],&p=0,\\\{1\},&p<0.\end{cases}\] The mapping \(S\) is outer semicontinuous but not lower semicontinuous, and hence not Painlevé--Kuratowski continuous, at \(p=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For this linear VI on an interval, every feasible point is a solution at zero, whereas only an endpoint is a solution at each nonzero nearby parameter; the solution map is outer semicontinuous but not lower semicontinuous at zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is not lower semicontinuous at \(p=0\), although it is outer semicontinuous there.

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy-Induced Discontinuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar generalized-equation example in which singular linearization coincides with loss of nearby solvability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The variational inequality is equivalent to \(x^2+p=0\), and its solution mapping is \[S(p)=\begin{cases}\{-\sqrt{-p},\sqrt{-p}\},&p<0,\\\{0\},&p=0,\\\varnothing,&p>0.\end{cases}\] At \((x,p)=(0,0)\), \(D_xF(0,0)=0\). The solution mapping has no nonempty-valued localization on a full neighborhood of \(p=0\); local solvability, a calm single-valued localization, and the Aubin property therefore fail at \((0,0)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Degenerate Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar boundary example separating continuity from Lipschitz stability at a singular solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The variational inequality is the equation \(x^3-p=0\), with unique solution mapping \(S(p)=\{p^{1/3}\}\) for every \(p\in\mathbb R\). At \((x,p)=(0,0)\), \(D_xF(0,0)=0\). The mapping \(S\) is continuous at \(p=0\) but is not locally Lipschitz there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cube-root solution map remains continuous at its singular reference solution, although it is not locally Lipschitz there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Degeneracy does not force discontinuity: \(S\) is continuous at \(0\) but is not locally Lipschitz there.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Strong metric subregularity of \(R\) at \((\bar x,0)\) means that there exist \(\kappa>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that \[\|x-\bar x\|\leq\kappa\,\operatorname{dist}(0,R(x))\qquad(x\in U).\] When \(R\) is single-valued, the right-hand side equals \(\kappa\|R(x)\|\). Thus the stability property supplies a pointwise error bound and makes \(\bar x\) an isolated zero of \(R\). The least admissible \(\kappa\) is the corresponding local error-bound modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong metric subregularity converts a small VI residual into a proportional bound on distance to an isolated reference solution.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT-Triple Error Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local residual bound for smooth inequality-and-equality constrained VI KKT systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z=(x,\lambda,\mu)\), define \[R_{\rm KKT}(z)=\bigl(F(x)+\nabla g(x)^\top\lambda+\nabla h(x)^\top\mu,\ h(x),\ \min\{\lambda,-g(x)\}\bigr),\] where the minimum is componentwise, and let \(Z^*=\{z:\lambda\geq0,\ R_{\rm KKT}(z)=0\}\). A local KKT-triple error bound at \(\bar z\in Z^*\) holds if there exist \(\kappa>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\leq\kappa\|R_{\rm KKT}(z)\|\] whenever \(\lambda\geq0\) and \(\|z-\bar z\|<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a reference KKT triple, a KKT-triple error bound controls distance to the KKT-triple set by the stationarity, feasibility, and complementarity residual.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) are continuously differentiable.
\((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\) is a KKT triple with \(\bar\lambda\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A KKT-triple error bound is \(\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\leq\kappa\|R_{\rm KKT}(z)\|\) locally around \(\bar z\).

knowledge_statements.title: Linearly Constrained Composite-VI Error Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-equation error bound for a convex composite VI over linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z=(x,\lambda)\), define \[H(z)=\bigl(F(x)+\partial g(x)+A^\top\lambda,\ b-Ax+N_{\mathbb R_+^m}(\lambda)\bigr).\] The inclusion \(0\in H(z)\) represents the composite VI condition \(0\in F(x)+\partial g(x)+N_C(x)\) together with a compatible multiplier. If \(H\) is metrically subregular at \((\bar z,0)\), then there exist \(\kappa>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(z,H^{-1}(0))\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,H(z))\] whenever \(\|z-\bar z\|<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity of the composite primal-dual KKT mapping bounds local solution distance by its stationarity and linear-complementarity residual.
assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Metric subregularity of \(H\) at \((\bar z,0)\) yields \(\operatorname{dist}(z,H^{-1}(0))\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,H(z))\) locally.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pointwise error bound for \(R(x)=0\) at \(\bar x\in S\) holds if there exist constants \(\kappa>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\|R(x)\|\qquad\text{whenever }\|x-\bar x\|<\varepsilon.\] For a set-valued residual, \(\|R(x)\|\) is replaced by \(\operatorname{dist}(0,R(x))\). The infimum of all admissible \(\kappa\) over possibly smaller neighborhoods is the pointwise error-bound modulus at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointwise error bound controls distance to the solution set by residual size only for points near one designated solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local natural-residual error bound for structured strongly monotone VIs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter-pointwise local error bound for a polyhedral variational inequality with a composite operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}, let K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be polyhedral, and let G:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^m be strongly monotone and Lipschitz continuous on \operatorname{range}(A). For b\in\mathcal{R}(K,G,A), define F(x)=A^TG(Ax)+b. Then there exist \eta,\delta>0, depending on b, such that \|\mathbf F_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(x)\|\leq\delta implies \operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{SOL}(K,F))\leq\eta\|\mathbf F_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(x)\|. Consequently, the VI (K,G,A,b) is semistable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each admissible parameter b, the structured polyhedral VI has a local linear distance bound in terms of its natural residual and is consequently semistable.
assumptions_latex: G:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^m\text{ is strongly monotone and Lipschitz continuous on }\operatorname{range}(A)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\eta,\delta>0:\ \|\mathbf F_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(x)\|\leq\delta\Rightarrow\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{SOL}(K,F))\leq\eta\|\mathbf F_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(x)\|;\quad (K,G,A,b)\text{ is semistable}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: R-zero criterion for a local natural-residual VI error bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A multiplier-wise sufficient criterion, with a converse under isolation and CRCQ or uniqueness of the extended multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K be a finitely representable convex set of the stated form, where h is affine and every g_i is convex and twice continuously differentiable. Let F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n be continuously differentiable, and let x^*\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F) satisfy SBCQ. If, for every (\mu,\lambda)\in\mathcal M^e(x^*), the pair \bigl(\mathcal C,J_x\mathbf L(x^*,\lambda)\bigr) is an R_0 pair, then \operatorname{SOL}(K,F) has a Lipschitzian error bound near x^* with residual \|\mathbf F_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(x)\|. Conversely, if x^* is isolated and either CRCQ holds or \mathcal M^e(x^*) is a singleton, then that error bound implies the R_0 condition for every (\mu,\lambda)\in\mathcal M^e(x^*).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an SBCQ solution of a smoothly represented convex VI, the multiplier-wise R-zero condition implies a local natural-residual error bound. For an isolated solution, the converse requires CRCQ or a unique extended multiplier.
assumptions_latex: K\text{ has the stated finite convex representation with }h\text{ affine and each }g_i\in C^2
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\forall(\mu,\lambda)\in\mathcal M^e(x^*),\ (\mathcal C,J_x\mathbf L(x^*,\lambda))\text{ is an }R_0\text{ pair}\bigr]\Rightarrow\text{the stated local error bound};\quad\text{the converse holds if }x^*\text{ is isolated and }\bigl(\mathrm{CRCQ}\text{ holds or }\mathcal M^e(x^*)\text{ is a singleton}\bigr).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local compound-residual error bound for structured strongly monotone VIs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter-pointwise distance estimate combining the natural residual with transformed-variable deviation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}, let K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be polyhedral, and let G:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^m be strongly monotone and Lipschitz continuous on \operatorname{range}(A). For b\in\mathcal{R}(K,G,A), define F(x)=A^TG(Ax)+b. Then there exist \eta_1,\delta_1>0, depending on b, such that \|\mathbf F_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(x)\|\leq\delta_1 implies \operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{SOL}(K,F))\leq\eta_1\left(\|\mathbf F_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(x)\|+\|Ax-v(b)\|\right).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each admissible parameter b, sufficiently small natural residual bounds the distance to the VI solution set by the natural residual plus the discrepancy between Ax and v(b).
assumptions_latex: G:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^m\text{ is strongly monotone and Lipschitz continuous on }\operatorname{range}(A)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\eta_1,\delta_1>0:\ \|\mathbf F_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(x)\|\leq\delta_1\Rightarrow\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{SOL}(K,F))\leq\eta_1\left(\|\mathbf F_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(x)\|+\|Ax-v(b)\|\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semistability and a natural-residual error bound at an isolated VI solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise equivalence localized at an isolated solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be closed and convex, let x^*\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F) be an isolated solution, and suppose F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n is Lipschitz continuous in a neighborhood of x^*. Then x^* is semistable if and only if \operatorname{SOL}(K,F) admits a Lipschitzian error bound near x^* with residual \|\mathbf F_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(x)\|.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an isolated variational-inequality solution, local Lipschitz continuity of the mapping makes semistability equivalent to a nearby Lipschitz error bound based on the natural residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ is semistable}\iff\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\text{ has a Lipschitzian natural-residual error bound near }x^*.

children.title: Local-Neighborhood Error Bounds
children.top_down_role: Error-bound behavior valid over a neighborhood of the solution set.

assumptions_latex: \(R:X\rightrightarrows Y\) is a set-valued residual mapping between normed spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One pair \((\kappa,varepsilon)\) controls the error bound around every solution in \(S\cap B_\varepsilon(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform local bound over all solutions in a neighborhood of the reference solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A local-neighborhood error bound at \(\bar x\in S\) holds if there exist \(\kappa>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that, for every \(u\in S\cap B_\varepsilon(\bar x)\) and every \(x\in B_\varepsilon(u)\), \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,R(x)).\] The same constants must work uniformly for all nearby centers \(u\). This is stronger than merely assigning a possibly different pointwise modulus and neighborhood to each individual solution near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A neighborhood error bound uses common constants to control residual error around every solution sufficiently close to the reference solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz LCP Residues Bound Residual by Solution Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A domain-uniform lower estimate for distance in terms of any Lipschitz LCP residue.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\operatorname{SOL}(q,M)\neq\varnothing\). If the residue \(r(\cdot,q,M):\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}_+\) is Lipschitz continuous on \(\mathcal D\supseteq S\) with modulus \(\widetilde c(q,M)>0\), then \[\widetilde c(q,M)^{-1}r(x,q,M)\leq\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal D.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a domain containing a nonempty LCP solution set, a Lipschitz residue divided by its Lipschitz modulus cannot exceed the distance to that solution set.
assumptions_latex: r(\cdot,q,M)\text{ is Lipschitz continuous on }\mathcal D\text{ with modulus }\widetilde c(q,M)>0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in\mathcal D,\quad \widetilde c(q,M)^{-1}r(x,q,M)\leq\operatorname{dist}(x,S)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact-domain globalization of a local natural-residual error bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local-to-global result for VI solution-set error bounds, including its compact-polyhedral AVI consequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be compact and convex, let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous, and let \(S=\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\). If \(S\) admits a local Lipschitzian error bound with the natural residual, then \(S\) admits a global Lipschitzian error bound with the same residual. Consequently, the solution set of every solvable affine variational inequality on a compact polyhedron admits a global Lipschitzian error bound with the natural residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous variational inequality on a compact convex set, a local Lipschitz error bound using the natural residual extends globally. Consequently, the result applies to every solvable affine VI on a compact polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is compact and convex}.
S=\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\text{ admits a local Lipschitzian error bound with the natural residual}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ admits a global Lipschitzian error bound with the natural residual; in particular, so does every solvable AVI on a compact polyhedron}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine VI global error bounds and Lipschitz solution maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between a uniform projection-residual error bound and global Lipschitz stability for affine variational inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be closed and convex and M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}. The following are equivalent: (i) there exists c>0 such that, for every q\in\mathcal{R}(K,M) and x\in\mathbb{R}^n, \[\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M))\le c\|x-\Pi_K(x-q-Mx)\|;\] (ii) (K,M) is a Lipschitzian pair, meaning that some c'>0 satisfies, for all q,q'\in\mathcal{R}(K,M), \[\operatorname{SOL}(K,q',M)\subseteq\operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M)+c'\|q-q'\|\,\operatorname{cl}\mathbb{B}.\] If K is polyhedral and \mathcal{R}(K,M)=\mathbb{R}^n, these conditions are also equivalent to \operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M) being a singleton for every q\in\mathbb{R}^n.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an affine variational inequality over a closed convex set, a uniform global error bound in terms of the projection residual is equivalent to global Lipschitz stability of its solution map. If the set is polyhedral and every right-hand side is solvable, both are further equivalent to unique solvability for every right-hand side.
assumptions_latex: K\text{ is polyhedral and }\mathcal{R}(K,M)=\mathbb{R}^n\text{ for the singleton equivalence}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Uniform projection-residual error bound}\iff\text{Lipschitzian pair};\quad K\text{ polyhedral and }\mathcal{R}(K,M)=\mathbb{R}^n\implies\bigl(\text{these}\iff\forall q\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ |\operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M)|=1\bigr).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global natural-residual error-bound criterion for a polyhedral affine VI
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes global natural-residual error bounds for a solvable polyhedral affine variational inequality through recession geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be polyhedral, \(M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and \(q\in\mathcal R(K,M)\). There exists \(c>0\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}\bigl(x,\operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M)\bigr)\le c\left\|x-\Pi_K(x-q-Mx)\right\|\quad\forall x\in\mathbb R^n\] if and only if \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M)_\infty=\mathcal K(K,M)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a solvable affine variational inequality on a polyhedral set, a global distance bound by the natural residual exists exactly when the recession cone of the solution set equals the associated characteristic cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left[\exists c>0\ \forall x\in\mathbb R^n:\operatorname{dist}\bigl(x,\operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M)\bigr)\le c\left\|x-\Pi_K(x-q-Mx)\right\|\right]\iff \operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M)_\infty=\mathcal K(K,M)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: R0 criterion for global natural-residual bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates the R0 property of a polyhedral affine-VI pair to global Lipschitzian natural-residual error bounds over all solvable right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be polyhedral and \(M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\). If \((K,M)\) is an \(R_0\) pair, then for every \(q\in\mathcal R(K,M)\), a global Lipschitzian error bound for \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M)\) holds in terms of the natural residual of \((K,q,M)\). Conversely, if this bound holds for every \(q\in\mathcal R(K,M)\) and there exists \(\bar q\in\mathcal R(K,M)\) such that \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,\bar q,M)\) is bounded, then \((K,M)\) is an \(R_0\) pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The R0 property guarantees a global natural-residual error bound for every solvable right-hand side. The converse requires the additional existence of a solvable right-hand side with a bounded solution set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (K,M)\text{ is }R_0\Rightarrow\forall q\in\mathcal R(K,M),\text{ a global natural-residual error bound holds};\quad \left[\forall q\in\mathcal R(K,M),\text{ such a bound holds}\ \land\ \exists\bar q\in\mathcal R(K,M):\operatorname{SOL}(K,\bar q,M)\text{ is bounded}\right]\Rightarrow (K,M)\text{ is }R_0

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone VI Global Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-sharpness global bound for a finite-dimensional monotone VI using the primal gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(G(x)=\sup_{y\in K}\langle F(x),x-y\rangle\) and let \(S\) be the VI solution set. If there exists \(\alpha>0\) such that \(\langle F(x^*),x-x^*\rangle\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\) for every \(x\in K\) and every \(x^*\in P_S(x)\), then \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\frac{G(x)}{\alpha}\qquad\text{for every }x\in K.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous monotone VI satisfying the stated weak-sharpness condition, the primal gap globally bounds distance to the solution set with constant one over the sharpness modulus.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(F:K\to\mathbb R^n\) is continuous and monotone.
The VI solution set \(S\) is nonempty, and the primal gap \(G(x)\) is finite for every \(x\in K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Affine VI Global Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample showing that affinity and polyhedral feasibility alone do not ensure a global natural-residual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine VI on \(K=\mathbb R_+\) with \(F(x)=1\) has solution set \(S=\{0\}\) and natural residual \[r(x)=x-P_K(x-1)=\begin{cases}x,&0\leq x\leq1,\\1,&x\geq1.\end{cases}\] Hence \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)=x\) while \(|r(x)|=1\) for \(x\geq1\), and no finite \(\kappa\) satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa|r(x)|\) for every \(x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant affine monotone VI on a polyhedral set can have bounded natural residual while distance to its solution set grows without bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite \(\kappa\) satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa|r(x)|\) for every \(x\in K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Affine VI Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global inclusion-residual bound for the strongly monotone subclass of affine VIs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The VI for \(F(x)=Mx+q\) on \(K\) has a unique solution \(x^*\). For every \(x\in K\), \[\|x-x^*\|\leq\frac{1}{\mu}\operatorname{dist}(0,F(x)+N_K(x)).\] Thus the inclusion residual gives a global error bound with modulus at most \(1/\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strongly monotone affine VI has a unique solution, and its inclusion residual globally bounds solution distance with constant one over the monotonicity modulus.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(F(x)=Mx+q\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unique solution \(x^*\) satisfies \(\|x-x^*\|\leq\operatorname{dist}(0,F(x)+N_K(x))/\mu\) for every \(x\in K\).

notation.meaning: Zero set of the residual in \(K\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-set global bound for a subanalytic VI residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact and let \(r:U\to[0,\infty)\) be continuous and subanalytic on an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(K\). If \(S:=\{x\in K:r(x)=0\}\) is nonempty, then there exist constants \(c>0\) and \(\theta\in(0,1]\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le c\,r(x)^\theta\qquad\text{for every }x\in K.
\]
Thus an analytic or subanalytic VI formulation has a Hölder global error bound on each compact region where its chosen nonnegative residual has exactly the solution set as its zero set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous subanalytic residual controls distance to its zero set by a Hölder power uniformly on any fixed compact region.
knowledge_statements.title: Analytic-Problem Global Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compact-set Hölder bound is mathematically plausible as a subanalytic Łojasiewicz-type error bound and fits the theorem container, but no source is supplied for the required hypotheses or exponent conclusion.

assumptions_latex: Strict complementarity holds: \(\bar\lambda_i>0\) exactly when \(g_i(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(0<\tau<\min_{i\in A(\bar x)}\bar\lambda_i\), one has \(A_k(\tau)=A(\bar x)\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite identification by convergent multipliers under strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose constraints are represented near \(\bar x\) by \(g_i(x)\le0\), and a primal-multiplier sequence satisfies \((x^k,\lambda^k)\to(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\). Assume strict complementarity in the form
\[
\bar\lambda_i>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad g_i(\bar x)=0.
\]
For any threshold \(\tau\) satisfying \(0<\tau<\min_{i\in A(\bar x)}\bar\lambda_i\), define \(A_k(\tau):=\{i:\lambda_i^k>\tau\}\). Then there exists \(k_0\) such that \(A_k(\tau)=A(\bar x)\) for every \(k\ge k_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergent multipliers identify the exact active constraints after finitely many iterations when strict complementarity holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Constraint Identification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The threshold-identification argument is plausible under multiplier convergence and strict complementarity, but it has no source. A source should also clarify the intended nonempty active-set case, since the displayed minimum is undefined when the active set is empty.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty closed convex subset of a Hilbert space \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(F,C)\) if and only if \(0\in F(x)+\rho\,\partial d_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise exact distance penalization at feasible VI candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be nonempty, closed, and convex in a Hilbert space \(H\), and let \(d_C\) denote distance to \(C\). For any \(x\in C\) and any \(\rho\ge\|F(x)\|\),
\[
\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\quad\text{for all }y\in C
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
0\in F(x)+\rho\,\partial d_C(x).
\]
Accordingly, the nonsmooth distance term is exact at every feasible candidate once the penalty parameter dominates the norm of the VI operator there. The assertion is pointwise and does not claim that every stationary point of the unconstrained penalized inclusion is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point, a distance penalty reproduces the VI condition once its parameter dominates the operator norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Penalization for VIs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise equivalence follows from the feasible-point formula for the convex subdifferential of the distance function and is appropriately limited to feasible candidates, but the record supplies no supporting citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a Hilbert space \(H\), with metric projection \(P_C\), and let \(F:H\to H\). The natural residual of the variational inequality is
\[
R_N(x):=x-P_C\bigl(x-F(x)\bigr),\qquad x\in H.
\]
Its norm is a computable stationarity measure. In particular,
\[
R_N(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x\in C\ \text{ and }\ \langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\ \text{for every }y\in C.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The natural residual is the displacement from a point to its projected forward step, and it vanishes exactly at VI solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Natural Residual

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex in a Hilbert space \(H\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter II. Variational Inequalities in Hilbert Space p. 23

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty closed convex set \(C\) in a Hilbert space \(H\), a map \(F:H\to H\), and a fixed scale \(\alpha>0\), define
\[
R_\alpha(x):=x-P_C\bigl(x-\alpha F(x)\bigr).
\]
The projection optimality condition gives the scale-independent zero-set identity
\[
R_\alpha(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x\in C\ \text{ and }\ \langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\ \text{for every }y\in C.
\]
Thus changing a fixed positive scale changes residual magnitudes but not the certified VI solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every fixed positive projection scale yields the same residual zero set, although residual magnitudes depend on the scale.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Projection Residuals

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(H(x)\) be symmetric positive definite and let \(P_C^{H(x)}\) denote projection onto \(C\) in the norm induced by \(H(x)\). Define
\[
R_H(x):=x-P_C^{H(x)}\bigl(x-H(x)^{-1}F(x)\bigr).
\]
Then
\[
R_H(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x\in C\ \text{ and }\ \langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\ \text{for every }y\in C.
\]
Pointwise positive definiteness is sufficient for this zero-set equivalence; uniform metric bounds are needed only for uniform norm comparisons and error estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite point-dependent metric preserves the VI residual zero set, though uniform estimates require stronger metric control.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Projection Residuals

children.title: Metric-Variation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Distinctions between fixed scaling and state-dependent metric choices.

assumptions_latex: Variable metrics are symmetric positive definite but lack a uniform upper spectral bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No constant \(c\) uniformly satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le c\|R_{H_k}(x)\|\) for all metrics in the family.

notation.meaning: Solution set of the example VI.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of uniform error bounds when metric spectra are unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Pointwise positive definiteness does not ensure metric-uniform residual bounds. Consider \(C=\mathbb{R}\), \(F(x)=x\), and \(H_k=kI\). The VI solution set is \(S=\{0\}\), while the variable-metric projection residual is
\[
R_{H_k}(x)=x-P_C^{H_k}\bigl(x-H_k^{-1}F(x)\bigr)=\frac{x}{k}.
\]
At \(x=1\), one has \(\operatorname{dist}(1,S)=1\) but \(\lvert R_{H_k}(1)\rvert=1/k\to0\). Hence no metric-independent constant \(c\) can satisfy \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le c\lVert R_{H_k}(x)\rVert\) throughout this family. A uniform upper spectral bound is therefore necessary for such a comparison in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unbounded metric eigenvalues can drive residuals to zero away from the solution set, destroying metric-uniform error bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Variation Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is internally correct and the failure_boundary kind exactly fits the leaf, but the record has no source for the general metric-variation boundary claim.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex in a Hilbert space \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_C^{\mathrm{nor}}(z)=0\) if and only if \(P_C(z)\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(F,C)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-map equation associated with a closed convex VI.

source_refs.locator: Chapter II. Variational Inequalities in Hilbert Space p. 23
source_refs.source_title: An Introduction to Variational Inequalities and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_C\) be the metric projection onto a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subset H\). For \(z\in H\), set \(x(z):=P_C(z)\) and define the normal map
\[
F_C^{\mathrm{nor}}(z):=F\bigl(x(z)\bigr)+z-x(z).
\]
Then
\[
F_C^{\mathrm{nor}}(z)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x(z)\in C\ \text{ and }\ \langle F(x(z)),y-x(z)\rangle\ge0\ \text{for every }y\in C.
\]
Thus a zero of the unconstrained normal-map residual projects to a VI solution; conversely, every VI solution \(x\) is obtained from \(z=x-F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal map converts the VI into an unconstrained equation whose zeros project exactly to VI solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Map Residual

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\varphi:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, let \(F:H\to H\), and fix \(\gamma>0\). Define
\[
R_\gamma^{\mathrm{prox}}(x):=\gamma^{-1}\left[x-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\varphi}\bigl(x-\gamma F(x)\bigr)\right].
\]
Then
\[
R_\gamma^{\mathrm{prox}}(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
0\in F(x)+\partial\varphi(x).
\]
When \(\varphi\) is the indicator of a closed convex set \(C\), the proximal mapping becomes \(P_C\), so this residual reduces to the scaled projection residual divided by \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forward-proximal displacement vanishes exactly at solutions of the generalized VI involving a convex subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Residuals

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_\gamma^A(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in F(x)+A(x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone, let \(F:H\to H\), and fix \(\gamma>0\). With resolvent \(J_{\gamma A}:=(I+\gamma A)^{-1}\), define
\[
R_\gamma^A(x):=\gamma^{-1}\left[x-J_{\gamma A}\bigl(x-\gamma F(x)\bigr)\right].
\]
The resolvent is everywhere single-valued, and
\[
R_\gamma^A(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
0\in F(x)+A(x).
\]
Hence the residual norm supplies a fixed-point certificate for the monotone inclusion representing the generalized variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The forward-resolvent displacement is zero exactly when the associated maximal-monotone inclusion is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent Residuals

children.title: Proximal–Resolvent Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between proximal and resolvent residual forms.

assumptions_latex: \(\varphi:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\varphi}=J_{\gamma\partial\varphi}\) and \(R_\gamma^{\mathrm{prox}}=R_\gamma^{\partial\varphi}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex proximal maps as subdifferential resolvents.

source_refs.locator: Chapter III. Variational Inequalities for Monotone Operators p. 83
source_refs.source_title: An Introduction to Variational Inequalities and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every proper lower-semicontinuous convex function \(\varphi:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and every \(\gamma>0\), its subdifferential is maximal monotone and
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\varphi}=(I+\gamma\partial\varphi)^{-1}=J_{\gamma\partial\varphi}.
\]
Consequently, for any single-valued map \(F:H\to H\),
\[
R_\gamma^{\mathrm{prox}}(x)=\gamma^{-1}\left[x-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\varphi}(x-\gamma F(x))\right]
=R_\gamma^{\partial\varphi}(x).
\]
Thus the proximal and resolvent residual formulations are identical when the monotone operator is a convex subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex functions, the proximal map is exactly the subdifferential resolvent, so their residual formulas coincide.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(C=\mathbb{R}_+^n\), the variational inequality for \(F\) is equivalent to
\[
x\ge0,\qquad F(x)\ge0,\qquad x_iF_i(x)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).
\]
It is also equivalent to the natural-residual equation
\[
x-[x-F(x)]_+=0.
\]
Define \(\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(a,b):=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}-a-b\) and \((\Phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x))_i:=\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x_i,F_i(x))\). Then
\[
\Phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x\text{ solves }\operatorname{VI}(F,\mathbb{R}_+^n).
\]
These equations provide the residual interface between VI and complementarity formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the nonnegative orthant, VI solutions are exactly complementarity solutions and zeros of projection or Fischer–Burmeister residuals.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Residual Interface

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularized gap certificate for a generalized quasi-variational inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the quadratic regularized gap for a GQVI and states its nonnegativity, attainment, and zero-gap characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \((x,v)\in\operatorname{gph}_{K}\Phi\) and \(c>0\), define
\[
\theta_c(x,v):=\max_{y\in K(x)}\left\{v^\top(x-y)-\frac c2\|y-x\|^2\right\}.
\]
If \(K(x)\neq\varnothing\) is closed, this maximum is attained and \(\theta_c(x,v)\geq0\). If, in addition, \(K(x)\) is convex, then
\[
\theta_c(x,v)=0\iff v^\top(y-x)\geq0\quad\forall y\in K(x).
\]
Thus \((x,v)\in\operatorname{gph}_{K}\Phi\) solves \(\operatorname{GQVI}(K,\Phi)\) exactly when \(\theta_c(x,v)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible GQVI pair, the regularized gap maximizes a linear violation term minus a quadratic term over K(x). A nonempty closed value K(x) ensures attainment and nonnegativity; convexity makes zero gap equivalent to the variational inequality.
assumptions_latex: K(x)\text{ is convex for the zero-gap equivalence}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \theta_c(x,v)\geq0,\qquad \theta_c(x,v)=0\iff v^\top(y-x)\geq0\ \forall y\in K(x).

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Gap Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-metric proximal regularization in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in C\), define \[g_{c,M}(x):=\max_{y\in C}\left\{\langle F(x),x-y\rangle-\frac{c}{2}\|x-y\|_M^2\right\},\qquad \|z\|_M^2:=\langle Mz,z\rangle.\] Its unique maximizer is \[y_{c,M}(x)=P_C^M\left(x-c^{-1}M^{-1}F(x)\right).\] Moreover, \[g_{c,M}(x)\geq0,\qquad g_{c,M}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\operatorname{Sol}(C,F).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite metric defines a proximal regularized gap whose unique maximizer is a metric projection and whose feasible zeros are exactly the variational-inequality solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive definite and \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal gap is attained at \(P_C^M(x-c^{-1}M^{-1}F(x))\), is nonnegative on \(C\), and vanishes exactly at VI solutions.

notation.meaning: norm induced by the positive-definite matrix M

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Gap Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bregman regularization with divergence oriented from the trial point to the base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,y\in C\), define \[D_h(y,x):=h(y)-h(x)-\langle\nabla h(x),y-x\rangle.\] For \(x\in C\), define the extended-real Bregman gap by \[g_{c,h}(x):=\sup_{y\in C}\left\{\langle F(x),x-y\rangle-cD_h(y,x)\right\}.\] Then \[g_{c,h}(x)\geq0,\qquad g_{c,h}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\operatorname{Sol}(C,F).\] If the supremum is attained, its maximizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Bregman gap penalizes trial points by a strictly convex Bregman divergence. It may be extended-valued, is nonnegative, and has exactly the variational-inequality solutions as feasible zeros; any attained maximizer is unique.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and strictly convex on an open set containing \(C\), and \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in C\), \(g_{c,h}(x)\geq0\), and \(g_{c,h}(x)=0\) exactly when \(x\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(C,F)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman–Proximal Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic Bregman generators recover fixed-metric proximal gaps exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(h_M(z):=\frac12\langle Mz,z\rangle\), the associated Bregman divergence is \[D_{h_M}(y,x)=\frac12\langle M(y-x),y-x\rangle=\frac12\|y-x\|_M^2.\] Consequently, for every \(x\in C\), \[g_{c,h_M}(x)=\sup_{y\in C}\left\{\langle F(x),x-y\rangle-\frac{c}{2}\|x-y\|_M^2\right\}=g_{c,M}(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a quadratic generator induced by a positive-definite matrix, the Bregman divergence is one half of the squared metric norm, so the Bregman gap equals the fixed-metric proximal gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{h_M}(y,x)=\frac12\|y-x\|_M^2\) and \(g_{c,h_M}(x)=g_{c,M}(x)\) for every \(x\in C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuity, exactness, and gradient of the D-gap function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuity, nonnegativity, exact zero certificate, and conditional differentiability of the established D-gap function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n be continuous, let K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be closed and convex, and let b>a>0. Then \theta_{ab} is continuous on \mathbb{R}^n, \theta_{ab}(x)\geq0 for every x, and \theta_{ab}(x)=0 if and only if x\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F). If F is continuously differentiable, then \theta_{ab} is continuously differentiable and \nabla\theta_{ab}(x)=JF(x)^T\bigl(y_b(x)-y_a(x)\bigr)+aG\bigl(y_a(x)-x\bigr)-bG\bigl(y_b(x)-x\bigr).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For continuous F and closed convex K, the D-gap function is continuous and nonnegative, and its zeros are exactly the VI solutions. If F is continuously differentiable, the D-gap function is continuously differentiable with the stated gradient.
assumptions_latex: \theta_{ab},\ y_a,\ y_b,\text{ and }G\text{ are those of the established D-gap construction}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \theta_{ab}\in C(\mathbb{R}^n),\quad \forall x:\ \theta_{ab}(x)\geq0,\quad \theta_{ab}(x)=0\iff x\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F);\quad F\in C^1\Rightarrow \theta_{ab}\in C^1\text{ and }\nabla\theta_{ab}(x)=JF(x)^T(y_b(x)-y_a(x))+aG(y_a(x)-x)-bG(y_b(x)-x).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative sufficient conditions for global coercivity: quantitative monotonicity of the mapping or boundedness of the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex and let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous. knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local solution-distance estimate and its stated positive-definiteness consequence for the second-order generalized differential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex, and let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be Lipschitz continuous in a neighborhood of a semistable solution \(x^*\) of \(\operatorname{VI}(K,F)\). knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Affine-Constraint Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete recession-direction boundary for D-gap coercivity on an unbounded affine set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\mathbb{R}^2\), \(F(x_1,x_2)=(x_1,0)\), and \(0<a<b\). For \(g_c(x)=\sup_{y\in K}\{\langle F(x),x-y\rangle-\tfrac c2\|x-y\|^2\}\) and \(D_{a,b}=g_a-g_b\), one has
\[
D_{a,b}(x)=\frac12\left(\frac1a-\frac1b\right)x_1^2.
\]
The VI solution set and the zero set of \(D_{a,b}\) are both \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:x_1=0\}\). Every nonempty sublevel set of \(D_{a,b}\) is unbounded in the \(x_2\)-direction, so zero validity does not imply coercivity or bounded merit sublevels on this unbounded affine set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In this affine example, the D-gap identifies the VI solutions exactly but is constant along an unbounded direction, making every nonempty sublevel unbounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{a,b}(x)=\tfrac12(a^{-1}-b^{-1})x_1^2\), and every nonempty sublevel set is unbounded in the \(x_2\)-direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Model Linearized Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional quadratic linearization using the symmetric Jacobian part.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in K\), let \(H_x=\tfrac12(F'(x)+F'(x)^{\mathsf T})\). If \(H_x\) is positive semidefinite on \(\operatorname{span}(K-K)\) and the displayed quadratic program has a finite attained minimum, the affine-model linearized gap is
\[
\ell(x):=-\min_{d\in K-x}\left\{\langle F(x),d\rangle+\frac12\langle d,H_xd\rangle\right\}.
\]
It is the negative optimal value of the convex quadratic affine model over feasible displacements and satisfies \(\ell(x)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine-model linearized gap is the negative finite minimum of the convex local quadratic model over feasible displacements.
assumptions_latex: The quadratic-model minimum is finite and attained
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell(x)=-\min_{d\in K-x}\{\langle F(x),d\rangle+\tfrac12\langle d,H_xd\rangle\}\ge0\).
